intro.en: An adverb made by adding -ly to a Latin-derived adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个由拉丁来源形容词加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The root prope, 'near', also lies behind proximity.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 prope「近」也是 proximity 的来源。

definition_zh: 围裙；停机坪；（舞台前缘的）台口
definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over the front of other clothes to keep them clean; also the area where aircraft park at an airport
core_image: 挡在前面的布：一块布挡在身前护住里面的衣服
scene: 妈妈系好围裙开始做饭。The chef put on an apron before starting to cook in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 apron 是「围裙」（第 1 个义项：护住身前的衣物）；句意为「厨师在下厨前系上了围裙」。该词还可指机场的停机坪或舞台前缘。

pos.zh: 停机坪（机场内飞机停放、装卸的区域）

collocations.phrase: wipe one's hands on the apron

derivatives.zh: apron 加形容词性后缀 -ed 构成，义为「系着围裙的」，多作定语描写人物形象
apron 加否定前缀 un- 与后缀 -ed 构成的少见形容词，义为「未系围裙的」，仅用于描写性语境

senses.title: A garment worn to protect clothes
senses.definition: a piece of cloth tied over the front of the body to keep the clothes underneath clean while cooking or working
senses.definitionCN: 系在身前的布片，做饭或干活时保护里面的衣服不被弄脏
senses.example: Grandma wears a floral apron when she makes dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶包饺子时系着一条花围裙。
senses.why: The core image is cloth hung in front as a shield; this is the direct, oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是布片挡在身前作屏障；这是该词最直接、最古老的用法。

senses.title: A protective surface or strip resembling an apron
senses.titleCN: 类似围裙的护面或护带
senses.definition: a surface or strip that protects or covers something, shaped like the front protection of an apron
senses.definitionCN: 形似围裙前襟、起保护或覆盖作用的表面或条带
senses.example: The road was rebuilt with a concrete apron at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 道路重修时，入口处铺了混凝土护面。
senses.why: Something spread out in front to protect looks like an apron worn in front of the body.
senses.whyCN: 铺展在前方起保护作用之物，形似穿在身前作保护的围裙。

senses.title: The airport area where aircraft park
senses.definition: the hard-surfaced area of an airport where planes park, load, and are serviced
senses.definitionCN: 机场内飞机停放、装卸与维护的硬化地面区域
senses.example: Ground staff guided the plane to the apron after landing.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落后，地勤人员将它引导到停机坪。
senses.why: The paved area spreads out in front of the terminal like a protective apron around the aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 航站楼前的硬化场地铺展延伸，如围裙般环护飞机，故得此名。

senses.title: The front edge of a stage
senses.definition: the part of a stage that extends in front of the curtain toward the audience
senses.definitionCN: 舞台幕布之前、向观众席延伸的部分
senses.example: The actor stepped onto the apron to speak to the audience directly.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上台口，直接面向观众说话。
senses.why: The stage floor juts forward beyond the main area, apron-like, reaching toward the seats.
senses.whyCN: 台面向主舞台之外前伸，形如围裙的裙摆探向观众席。

intro.en: Apron is a famous case of a word losing an n: it came from napron through misdivision.
intro.cn: apron 是「丢失字母 n」的著名案例：由 napron 经错误切分而来。

items.en: Old French naperon, a diminutive of nape (tablecloth), from Latin mappa (cloth).
items.cn: 古法语 naperon，是 nape（桌布）的小称形式，源自拉丁语 mappa（布）。

items.en: Borrowed into Middle English as napron, meaning a small cloth or protecting cloth.
items.cn: 十四世纪进入中古英语，作 napron，义为小块布或护身之布。

items.en: a napron was misheard and re-cut as an apron, moving the n to the previous word; a napron became an apron.
items.cn: a napron 被误听并重新切分为 an apron，字母 n 移给了前一个冠词，napron 变成了 apron。

items.en: The new form apron established itself in the 1400s and 1500s and became the standard spelling.
items.cn: 新形式 apron 在十五至十六世纪站稳脚跟，成为标准拼写。

items.en: The sense spread from the kitchen garment to protective strips, the airport apron, and the stage apron.
items.cn: 词义从厨房围裙扩展到护面、机场停机坪和舞台台口。

note.en: Watch out for sound-alikes and related protective cloth words.
note.cn: 注意发音相近词及相关防护布类词。

entries.definition: a small cloth for wiping the mouth; shares the French root nape
entries.definitionCN: 餐巾；与 apron 同源于法语 nape（桌布）

entries.definition: table linen, an old word from the same French root
entries.definitionCN: 桌布餐巾类织物；源自同一法语词根的旧词

entries.definition: to try to do something; only the opening letters look similar
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；仅开头拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a loose protective garment, often worn by artists or workers
entries.definitionCN: 罩衫；宽松防护衣，多为画师或工人所穿

entries.definition: protective clothing worn over ordinary clothes, often with sleeves and legs
entries.definitionCN: 工装裤/罩衣；覆盖面比围裙更大的防护服

entries.definition: informal word for the airport parking area, near apron in sense 03
entries.definitionCN: 停机坪（口语说法），与 apron 第 3 义项近义

normalIntro.en: Remember the lost n and the picture of the cloth in front.
normalIntro.cn: 记住那个丢失的 n 和「挡身前的布」的画面。

normal.en: a napron -> an apron: the n jumped from the noun to the article.
normal.cn: a napron → an apron：字母 n 从名词跳到了冠词上。

normal.en: napkin and apron are cousins: both come from nape, the French word for tablecloth.
normal.cn: napkin 与 apron 是亲戚：都来自法语 nape（桌布）。

normal.en: apron strings is a fixed phrase: under one's apron strings means being controlled by someone.
normal.cn: apron strings（围裙带）是固定搭配，under one's apron strings 指「在某人掌控下」。

normal.en: Sound link: 'AY-pron' sounds like 'A-pron' — just the article A plus pron.
normal.cn: 读音联想「诶-普伦」：就像冠词 A 加 pron，好记它的来历。

normal.en: Airport apron: the ground apron-like in front of the terminal where planes park.
normal.cn: 机场停机坪：航站楼前铺展如围裙的地面，飞机停在那里。

abstract.en: Picture a shield made of cloth hanging in front of you.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布做的盾牌挂在身前。

abstract.en: Apron is protection you wear; armor is protection you fight in.
abstract.cn: apron 是穿着的防护，armor 是上阵的铠甲。

abstract.en: One n walked away from napron and never came back.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 n 从 napron 里出走，再也没有回来。

examples.en: She wiped her wet hands on her apron.
examples.cn: 她在围裙上擦了擦湿手。

examples.en: Pilots and ground crews work together on the apron.
examples.cn: 飞行员和地勤人员在停机坪上协同工作。

examples.en: An apron keeps oil stains off your clothes while cooking.
examples.cn: 做饭时围裙能防止油渍弄脏衣服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶铺龙」——诶，围裙一铺开像条小龙挡在身前，油点都溅不到衣服。

root: 源自拉丁语 mappa（布）→ 古法语 nape（桌布）→ naperon（小桌布，护身之布）→ 中古英语 napron → 因误切分 an apron 失去首字母 n。词形演变脉络清晰，misdivision（错误切分）是语言学上著名案例。

sensesIntro.en: From the cloth in front of the body, the word spreads to any apron-like protective area.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「身前的布」出发，词义扩展到一切形似围裙的防护区域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth spread in front as a protective shield
core.cn: 核心意象：铺展在身前、起保护作用的布

branches.en: The kitchen garment that keeps clothes clean.
Any protective surface shaped like a front shield.
The airport ground that spreads before the terminal.
branches.cn: 航站楼前铺展的机场停机坪。

branches.en: The stage floor reaching toward the audience.
branches.cn: 伸向观众席的舞台前缘。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of front protection.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「在前防护」的观念。

intro.en: Apron is a simple noun with few affixes; its story is in sound change, not building blocks.
intro.cn: apron 是个朴素的名词，几乎不用词缀；它的故事在语音演变，而非构词部件。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source mappa also gave the word map.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源 mappa 还派生出 map（地图）一词。

items.example: Mappa is the far source of apron.
items.exampleCN: mappa 是 apron 的远期词源。

items.example: Nape narrowed to mean linen cloth in Old French.
items.exampleCN: nape 在古法语中收窄为餐布之义。

items.example: Napron lost its n through misdivision.
items.exampleCN: napron 因误切分丢掉了首字母 n。

items.example: Napkin keeps the n that apron lost.
items.exampleCN: napkin 保留了 apron 丢失的 n。

items.example: Napery is an old word for household linen.
items.exampleCN: napery 是家用布艺的旧称。

items.example: The aproned cook stirred the soup.
items.exampleCN: 系着围裙的厨师搅动着汤。

latinEntries.example: Mappa mundi once meant a cloth map of the world.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mappa mundi 原指绘在布上的世界地图。

definition_zh: adj. 恰当的，贴切的；易于……的，有……倾向的；（学生）聪慧的，一学就会的
definition_en: Exactly suited to the purpose or occasion; inclined or liable to do something; of a learner, quick to pick things up.
core_image: 正好合得上那个槽口，一放就到位
scene: 这个比喻用得恰到好处。It was an apt metaphor for a fragile economy.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apt 指某句话或某个说法正好贴合眼下的情形，不多不少。

senses.title: Exactly suited
senses.definition: so well fitted to the situation that it seems made for it, used of words, names and comparisons
senses.definitionCN: 与情形贴合得仿佛专为它而造，用于词语、名称与比喻
senses.example: Silence was the aptest reply he could give.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默是他能给出的最贴切的回答。
senses.why: The Latin source means fastened or fitted, so an apt phrase is one that clicks into the situation like a part into its slot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「装好的、合上的」，所以 apt 的说法就像零件卡进槽口一样合上眼下的情形。

senses.title: Inclined or liable
senses.definition: having a tendency to do something, in the pattern apt to plus a verb
senses.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，用于 apt to 加动词的句式
senses.example: Old pipes are apt to burst in a hard frost.
senses.exampleCN: 旧水管在严寒中容易爆裂。
senses.why: If a thing fits a slot, it slides there easily, so fitted turns into likely: the behaviour is the groove it naturally runs in.
senses.whyCN: 东西合得上槽口就容易滑进去，于是「合上」引申为「易于」：那种行为就是它天然会走的沟槽。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: of a person, especially a pupil, ready and able to take in new skills
senses.definitionCN: 指人尤其是学生，能迅速接受新技能
senses.example: She was an apt student of the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她学小提琴一点就通。
senses.why: Here the fit is between the learner and the subject: the mind takes the shape of what it is taught without resistance.
senses.whyCN: 这里合得上的是学习者与所学：头脑毫无阻力地长成所教内容的形状。

intro.en: Apt is Latin aptus, fitted, the past participle of apere, to fasten. The same root gives adapt, adept, inept and aptitude.
intro.cn: apt 就是拉丁语 aptus「合好的」，是 apere「系紧、装上」的过去分词。同一词根产生 adapt、adept、inept 与 aptitude。

items.en: Latin apere meant to fasten or attach one thing to another, a verb of joining rather than of choosing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 apere 意为「把一物系到另一物上」，是表「连接」而非「挑选」的动词。

items.en: The participle aptus meant fastened, hence fitted and suitable: the part is already in its place.
items.cn: 过去分词 aptus 意为「系好的」，进而指「合适的」：零件已经就位。

items.en: Greek haptein, to fasten, is a cousin of apere, which shows the root is older than Latin itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 haptein「系紧」与 apere 同源，说明这个词根比拉丁语本身更古老。

items.en: English borrowed apt in the late fourteenth century for something suited to its purpose.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末借入 apt，表示某物与其用途相合。

items.en: Around the 1590s apt gained the sense of prone or liable, and also the sense of a quick learner.
items.cn: 1590 年代前后，apt 增加了「易于、往往」之义，也增加了「学得快」之义。

items.en: The same root builds adapt, to fit to, adept, thoroughly fitted, and inept, not fitted at all.
items.cn: 同一词根构成 adapt「使合上」、adept「完全合上、熟练」与 inept「完全合不上、笨拙」。

note.en: The look-alike group is a family lesson: adept is skilled, inept is clumsy, adapt is to make fit; the near-meaning group gives the plain synonyms.
note.cn: 形近组是一堂家族课：adept 是熟练，inept 是笨拙，adapt 是使合适；近义组给出朴素同义词。

entries.definition: To change so as to fit.
Likely to do or suffer something.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能做某事或遭遇某事。

normalIntro.en: Apt means fitted: a phrase that fits the moment, a habit that fits the person, a mind that fits the subject.
normalIntro.cn: apt 的本意是「合得上」：说法合得上此刻，习惯合得上这人，头脑合得上这门学问。

normal.en: Apt to plus a verb means likely to.
normal.cn: apt to 加动词意为「易于、往往」。

normal.en: Comparative and superlative are apter and aptest.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 apter、aptest。

normal.en: The adverb is aptly, as in aptly named.
normal.cn: 副词是 aptly，如 aptly named「名副其实」。

normal.en: Adept is skilled; inept is clumsy; do not mix them.
normal.cn: adept 是熟练，inept 是笨拙，别混。

normal.en: Apt is short and formal; suitable is the safe everyday word.
normal.cn: apt 简短而正式，suitable 是稳妥的日常词。

abstract.en: Picture a key sliding into its own lock.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙滑进属于它的那把锁。

abstract.en: Imagine a nickname that fits like a glove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴得像手套的外号。

abstract.en: Think of a groove a ball keeps rolling back into.
abstract.cn: 想象一条球总会滚回去的沟槽。

examples.en: The title is apt: the book really is about waiting.
examples.cn: 书名很贴切：这本书写的确实就是等待。

examples.en: He is apt to promise more than he can deliver.
examples.cn: 他往往承诺得比能做到的多。

examples.en: An apt pupil needs showing only once.
examples.cn: 一学就会的学生只需示范一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：apt 与 adapt 同根，本义「合得上」——话合得上场面就是贴切，人合得上学问就是聪慧。

root: 拉丁语 apere「系紧、装上」的过去分词 aptus「合好的」，经法语进入英语作 apt；由「合上槽口」引申出「贴切」「易于」与「学得快」三义。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses are one fit: words fitting a moment, a person fitting a habit, and a mind fitting a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一种「合上」：词语合上此刻，人合上某种习惯，头脑合上一门学问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part dropping straight into its own slot
core.cn: 核心意象：正好合得上那个槽口，一放就到位

branches.en: A nickname that fits perfectly.
Silence as the best reply.
Old pipes bursting in a frost.
A pupil who needs one demonstration.
Both slide easily into a groove.

intro.en: Apt is the fit root itself, and with ad-, in- and -itude it builds adapt, inept and aptitude.
intro.cn: apt 本身就是「合」词根，加上 ad-、in- 与 -itude 便构成 adapt、inept 与 aptitude。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is apere, to fasten, and its participle aptus, fitted; Greek haptein is the older cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 apere「系紧」及其分词 aptus「合好的」；希腊语 haptein 是更古老的同源词。

latinEntries.exampleCN: apere 是 apt 的来源。
aptus 产生 apt 与 adept。

latinEntries.example: Haptein is a cousin of apere.

definition_zh: n. 天资，天赋；（学习某事的）能力倾向；（考试测出的）潜能
definition_en: A natural ability to learn or do something well, present before training; in testing, the potential a person shows for a particular kind of work or study.
core_image: 还没学就已经对得上的那个槽口
scene: 她没上过课，却一学就会。She showed a real aptitude for languages.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aptitude 指训练之前就存在的天资，常与 for 连用指出在哪一方面。

senses.title: Natural readiness to learn
senses.definition: an inborn readiness for a particular skill, so that progress comes faster than training alone would explain
senses.definitionCN: 对某种技能天生的准备度，使进步快得超出训练本身所能解释的程度
senses.example: His aptitude for figures showed up before he could read.
senses.exampleCN: 他还不会认字时就显出了对数字的天赋。
senses.why: The word is apt plus -itude, the state of being fitted, so aptitude names a fit that exists before anyone teaches you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 apt 加 -itude，即「合得上的状态」，所以 aptitude 指的是在有人教你之前就已存在的那种契合。

senses.title: Measured potential
senses.definition: in education and hiring, the capacity a test estimates for future performance, as opposed to what has already been learnt
senses.definitionCN: 在教育与招聘中，指测试估出的未来表现潜力，与已学到的知识相对
senses.example: The firm replaced the interview with an aptitude test.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司用能力倾向测试取代了面试。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word to separate potential from achievement: aptitude looks forward, achievement looks back.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词把潜能与成绩分开：aptitude 朝前看，achievement 朝后看。

intro.en: Aptitude is Latin aptitudo, fitness, from aptus, fitted. Italian attitudine, from the same Latin word, gave English attitude, so the two are relatives.
intro.cn: aptitude 就是拉丁语 aptitudo「合适度」，来自 aptus「合好的」。意大利语 attitudine 出自同一拉丁词，产生了英语 attitude，所以两者是亲戚。

items.en: The chain starts with apere, to fasten, the verb behind apt, adapt and adept.
items.cn: 这条链从 apere「系紧」开始，它是 apt、adapt 与 adept 背后的动词。

items.en: Aptus, the participle, meant fitted or suitable, the state of a part already in place.
items.cn: 分词 aptus 意为「合好的、合适的」，即零件已经就位的状态。

items.en: Adding -tudo, the suffix for a state, gave aptitudo, fitness or suitability.
items.cn: 加上表状态的后缀 -tudo 得到 aptitudo「合适度、适合性」。

items.en: Italian turned the same word into attitudine, which reached English as attitude, a posture of mind.
items.cn: 意大利语把同一个词变成 attitudine，进入英语成 attitude，指心理姿态。

items.en: English took aptitude in the fifteenth century for fitness or natural tendency.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪吸收 aptitude，表示「适合性」或「天然倾向」。

items.en: From the 1920s psychologists used aptitude for measured potential, which gave the aptitude test.
items.cn: 自 1920 年代起，心理学家用 aptitude 指测出的潜能，于是有了能力倾向测试。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on attitude, a genuine relative that now means posture of mind, and altitude, which only looks similar; the near-meaning group lists words for talent.
note.cn: 形近组的核心是 attitude：真正的同源词，如今指心理姿态；还有只是形似的 altitude。近义组列出表示才能的词。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的看法或感受方式。

entries.definition: To change so as to fit.
Power to do something, learnt or not.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的能力，不论是否学来。

normalIntro.en: Aptitude is apt plus -itude: the state of already fitting, before any teaching begins.
normalIntro.cn: aptitude 就是 apt 加 -itude：在任何教学开始之前就已经合得上的那种状态。

normal.en: Use aptitude for plus the field: for languages.
normal.cn: 用 aptitude for 加领域：for languages。

normal.en: Aptitude is potential; achievement is what you learnt.
normal.cn: aptitude 是潜能，achievement 是已学到的。

normal.en: Attitude means outlook, not talent, despite the shared root.
normal.cn: attitude 指心态而非才能，尽管同源。

normal.en: The fixed pair is aptitude test, never aptitude exam.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 aptitude test，不说 aptitude exam。

normal.en: It can be countable: several distinct aptitudes.
normal.cn: 它可数：several distinct aptitudes。

abstract.en: Picture a slot already shaped for a part.
abstract.cn: 想象一个已按零件形状开好的槽口。

abstract.en: Imagine a child reading music before lessons.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子还没上课就能读谱。

abstract.en: Think of a test that guesses tomorrow, not yesterday.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预测明天而非清点昨天的测试。

examples.en: The school tests aptitude rather than memory.
examples.cn: 这所学校测的是潜能，而不是记忆。

examples.en: She has little aptitude for figures but great patience.
examples.cn: 她对数字没什么天赋，但极有耐心。

examples.en: His aptitudes were clear long before his grades were.
examples.cn: 他的天资早在成绩显现之前就一目了然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：apt「合得上」+ -itude「状态」——天生就合得上的状态，就是天资 aptitude。

root: 拉丁语 apere「装上」的分词 aptus「合好的」加状态后缀 -tudo 成 aptitudo「合适度」，经法语入英语作 aptitude；1920 年代心理学用它指测出的潜能。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a fit that comes before training: the talent you can see, and the same talent as a test score.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都指训练之前就存在的契合：看得见的天资，以及化作测试分数的同一份天资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the slot already matches before any lesson begins
core.cn: 核心意象：还没学就已经对得上的那个槽口

branches.en: A child reading music untaught.
branches.cn: 没人教就能读谱的孩子。

branches.en: A feel for numbers before school.
branches.cn: 上学前就对数字有感觉。

branches.en: A test that predicts future skill.
Hiring by potential, not by grades.
Both look at fit before training.
branches.cn: 两者看的都是训练前的契合。

intro.en: Aptitude is apt plus the state suffix -itude, which also builds altitude, magnitude and gratitude.
intro.cn: aptitude 是 apt 加状态后缀 -itude，同一后缀还构成 altitude、magnitude 与 gratitude。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is apere, aptus and aptitudo; Italian attitudine is the same word on a different road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 apere、aptus 与 aptitudo；意大利语 attitudine 是同一个词走了另一条路。

latinEntries.exampleCN: apere 是整个词族的起点。
aptus 产生 apt 与 aptitude。

definition_zh: n. 水族箱，鱼缸；水族馆（复数 aquariums 或 aquaria）
definition_en: A glass tank or pool in which fish and water plants are kept alive; also the building where such tanks are shown to the public.
core_image: 一面玻璃后面，水里的世界照常运转
scene: 孩子们隔着玻璃看鳐鱼滑过。The children watched rays glide across the aquarium.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aquarium 指养活水生物的玻璃缸或水池，也可指展出这些缸的整座场馆。

senses.title: A tank of living water
senses.definition: a glass container or small pool kept filled with water so that fish, plants and other water life can live in it
senses.definitionCN: 盛满水的玻璃容器或小池，供鱼类、水草及其他水生生物存活
senses.example: A balanced aquarium needs plants as well as fish.
senses.exampleCN: 一个平衡的水族箱既要有鱼，也要有水草。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a watering place, so the ending -arium still says place: a place made of water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原意是「饮水处」，所以词尾 -arium 仍在说「场所」：一个用水做成的场所。

senses.title: The building that shows them
senses.definition: a public institution where large tanks display sea and river life to visitors
senses.definitionCN: 用大型水箱向参观者展示海洋与河流生物的公共机构
senses.example: The city aquarium opens a jellyfish hall this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 市水族馆今春新开一个水母展厅。
senses.why: Once the tanks grew big enough to need a building, the place word stretched from the glass box to the whole hall.
senses.whyCN: 当水箱大到需要专门建筑时，这个表「场所」的词就从玻璃缸扩展到了整座展馆。

intro.en: Aquarium is Latin aquarium, a watering place for cattle, the neuter of aquarius, of water, from aqua, water. English borrowed it in 1853 for the new fish tanks.
intro.cn: aquarium 就是拉丁语 aquarium「牲畜饮水处」，是 aquarius「属于水的」的中性形式，来自 aqua「水」。英语在 1853 年借它来指新出现的鱼缸。

items.en: The reconstructed root akwa- meant water, and it also gives Old English ea, a river, seen in place names.
items.cn: 重构词根 akwa- 意为「水」，它也产生古英语 ea「河流」，保留在地名中。

items.en: Latin aqua meant water and gives aqua, aquatic, aqueduct and aquarelle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aqua 意为「水」，产生 aqua、aquatic、aqueduct 与 aquarelle。

items.en: The adjective aquarius meant of or for water, as in the water carrier of the zodiac.
items.cn: 形容词 aquarius 意为「属于水的、供水的」，如黄道十二宫中的持水者。

items.en: Its neuter form aquarium named a watering place for cattle, a place defined by its water.
items.cn: 其中性形式 aquarium 指「牲畜饮水处」，一个由水定义的场所。

items.en: In 1853 London opened a fish house and the Latin word was revived for the artificial tank.
items.cn: 1853 年伦敦开设鱼类展馆，这个拉丁词被重新起用来指人工水箱。

items.en: As tanks grew into halls, aquarium came to mean the whole public institution, not just the glass box.
items.cn: 随着水箱发展为展厅，aquarium 转而指整座公共机构，而不只是那只玻璃缸。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the water words and sets terrarium, the dry-land counterpart, beside aquarium; the near-meaning group lists other places for keeping animals.
note.cn: 形近组区分各个「水」词，并把陆生对应词 terrarium 与 aquarium 并列；近义组列出其他饲养展示动物的场所。

entries.definition: A glass case for plants or small land animals.
entries.definitionCN: 养植物或小型陆生动物的玻璃箱。

entries.definition: A place for keeping living creatures.

normalIntro.en: Aquarium is aqua, water, plus -arium, a place: a place made of water, whether a tank or a whole hall.
normalIntro.cn: aquarium 就是 aqua「水」加 -arium「场所」：用水做成的场所，小到一只缸，大到整座馆。

normal.en: Two plurals are correct: aquariums and aquaria.
normal.cn: 两种复数都对：aquariums 与 aquaria。

normal.en: Terrarium is the dry counterpart, with terra for earth.
normal.cn: terrarium 是陆生对应词，terra 意为「土」。

normal.en: Aquarium fish is a fixed pair for ornamental fish.
normal.cn: aquarium fish 是观赏鱼的固定说法。

normal.en: The stress sits on -quar-, /ˈkweə/.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -quar- 上，读 /ˈkweə/。

normal.en: The keeper is an aquarist, with -ist for a person.
normal.cn: 饲养者叫 aquarist，-ist 表人。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of river held behind glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一片被玻璃留住的河流切片。

abstract.en: Imagine a room where the walls are water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个四壁都是水的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a watering place for cattle turned into a tank.
abstract.cn: 想象牲畜饮水处变成了一只水箱。

examples.en: The aquarium keeps its coral at a steady temperature.
examples.cn: 水族馆把珊瑚养在恒定温度下。

examples.en: Both aquariums on the coast rescue injured turtles.
examples.cn: 海边这两家水族馆都救助受伤的海龟。

examples.en: The laboratory houses twelve aquaria for the study.
examples.cn: 实验室为这项研究放置了十二只水族缸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：aqua「水」+ -arium「场所」——装水的场所，小的是鱼缸，大的是水族馆 aquarium。

root: 原始印欧词根 akwa-「水」生出拉丁 aqua，形容词 aquarius「属于水的」的中性形式 aquarium 原指牲畜饮水处；1853 年英语重新起用指人工鱼缸，后扩展指水族馆。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one water place: the glass box that holds a living slice of water, and the building that holds many such boxes.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个「水的场所」：留住一片活水世界的玻璃缸，以及容纳许多这样缸的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: behind one pane of glass, the water world keeps running
core.cn: 核心意象：一面玻璃后面，水里的世界照常运转

branches.en: A planted tank on a desk.
branches.cn: 桌上一只种了水草的缸。

branches.en: A saltwater pool for coral.
A hall of jellyfish tanks.
A city institution that rescues turtles.
Both are places defined by water.
branches.cn: 两者都是由水定义的场所。

intro.en: Aquarium is aqua plus -arium, a place suffix; the same water root builds aquatic, aquifer, aqueduct and aquaculture.
intro.cn: aquarium 是 aqua 加场所后缀 -arium；同一「水」词根还构成 aquatic、aquifer、aqueduct 与 aquaculture。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is aqua, aquarius and aquarium; terra, earth, gives the contrasting terrarium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 aqua、aquarius 与 aquarium；terra「土」给出对照词 terrarium。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aqua 是所有「水」词的开头。

latinEntries.example: Aquarium once meant a cattle trough.

definition_zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的；（名词）水生生物
definition_en: living or growing in water, or connected with water, water environments and water sports
core_image: 睡莲的根扎在塘泥里，叶片浮出水面，水下的鱼在叶影间穿行
scene: 池塘里的睡莲把根扎在泥中，叶片浮在水面上。Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 aquatic 指「生长在水中的」（第 2 个义项：植物扎根水中或浮于水面）；句意：池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。图中可辨识物件：浮出水面的圆叶、塘底淤泥、游动的鱼、映着天光的池水。

pos.zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的
水生生物（常作复数 aquatics，指水生动植物或水上运动项目）

forms.label: 复数名词（水生生物／水上运动）

derivatives.zh: 水上运动项目；水生生物（总称）

senses.title: Animals that live in water
senses.definition: describing animals that spend their lives in water, whether fresh or salt
senses.definitionCN: 描述一生都在淡水或咸水中度过的动物
senses.example: Fish, turtles and frogs are aquatic animals with very different body plans.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼、龟和蛙都是水生动物，身体结构却大不相同。
senses.why: the Latin root aqua simply means water, so the adjective marks the medium an organism lives in rather than any particular body shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aqua 就是「水」，因此这个形容词标记的是生物生活的介质，而不是某种特定体型。

senses.title: Plants that grow in or on water
senses.titleCN: 扎根水中或浮在水面的植物
senses.definition: describing plants that root in water or mud below water and may float their leaves at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 描述根扎在水中或水下泥里、叶片可浮到水面的植物
senses.example: Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。
senses.why: botany extends the same medium-based label to plants, and the key contrast is with terrestrial, dry-land growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「按介质命名」的标签用于植物，关键对照是陆生的 dry-land 生长。

senses.title: Relating to water environments
senses.definition: connected with the physical or chemical conditions of rivers, lakes, wetlands and seas
senses.definitionCN: 与河流、湖泊、湿地和海洋的物理或化学条件有关
senses.example: The survey measured aquatic oxygen levels along the whole river.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了整条河的水体含氧量。
senses.why: once the word is detached from a particular organism it can describe any process or measurement whose setting is water.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词脱离具体生物，就可以描述任何以水为场景的过程或测量。

senses.title: Water sports and activities
senses.definition: connected with sports practised in or on water, such as swimming, rowing and diving
senses.definitionCN: 与在水中或水面上进行的运动有关，如游泳、划船和跳水
senses.example: The new centre hosts all aquatic events except open-water swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 新中心承办除公开水域游泳以外的全部水上项目。
senses.why: sports administration borrowed the adjective as a neutral cover term for events held in a pool or on a lake.
senses.whyCN: 体育管理借用这个形容词，作为在泳池或湖面上举行的项目的统称。

senses.title: A water-dwelling organism
senses.definition: a plant or animal that lives in water, often used in the plural for a collection of such organisms
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水中的植物或动物，复数常指一类水生生物的总称
senses.example: The reserve protects rare aquatics in the spring-fed pools.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区保护着这些泉水池中的珍稀水生生物。
senses.why: the noun is a straightforward conversion of the adjective, naming whatever the adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: 名词由形容词直接转化而来，指形容词所描述的那类事物。

senses.title: Kept in an aquarium
senses.definition: describing animals or plants kept in tanks for display or hobby use rather than in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述养在水箱中供展示或爱好之用、而非野生状态的动植物
senses.example: The shop sells aquatic supplies for both beginners and breeders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店为新手和繁殖者都提供水族用品。
senses.why: the hobby trade narrowed the adjective to tank-kept life, a smaller world that still shares the water medium.
senses.whyCN: 水族爱好把这个形容词收窄到水箱中的生物，范围更小，但介质仍是水。

senses.title: Of aquatic ecology as a field
senses.definition: used in ecology for studies of communities that live in water, as opposed to terrestrial ones
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中用于研究水中生物群落，与陆生群落相对
senses.example: Her thesis compares aquatic and terrestrial carbon cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文比较水生与陆生碳循环。
senses.why: the adjective became a standard term of division in ecology, pairing with terrestrial to split the living world by medium.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成为生态学的标准划分用语，与 terrestrial 配对，按介质把生物界一分为二。

senses.title: Rare figurative use: fluid and flowing
senses.titleCN: 罕见的修辞义：如水般流畅
senses.definition: rarely, describing movement or style that is smooth and flowing like water
senses.definitionCN: 罕见用法，形容动作或风格像水一样平滑流动
senses.example: Her aquatic grace on the beam surprised the judges.
senses.exampleCN: 她在平衡木上如水般的优雅让裁判惊讶。
senses.why: the metaphor is occasional and stylistic; dictionaries usually mark it as extended rather than a settled sense.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻只是偶发的修辞用法；词典通常把它标为引申用法，而非稳定义项。

intro.en: Aquatic comes from Latin aquaticus 'living in water', built on aqua 'water' plus the adjective suffix -aticus. It entered English in the early fifteenth century.
intro.cn: aquatic 来自拉丁 aquaticus「生活在水中的」，由 aqua「水」加形容词后缀 -aticus 构成，15 世纪初进入英语。

items.en: Aqua 'water' is one of the best-attested Latin nouns; its reconstructed Indo-European base is *akwa-, a form recovered by comparison rather than recorded anywhere.
items.cn: aqua「水」是拉丁语中记载最充分的名称之一；其重构的印欧语词根为 *akwa-，这一形式靠比较构拟，并无实际记录。

items.en: The suffix -aticus formed adjectives of place or belonging, so aquaticus meant 'of water, living in water'.
items.cn: 后缀 -aticus 构成表示场所或归属的形容词，因此 aquaticus 意为「水的、生活在水中的」。

items.en: English took the adjective in the early 1400s, at first in medical and natural-history writing about creatures and humours.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪初借入该形容词，最初见于医学与博物学著作，谈生物与体液。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries aquatic was applied to swimming, rowing and diving, giving the fixed phrase aquatic sports.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，aquatic 被用于游泳、划船与跳水，形成固定短语 aquatic sports。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology paired aquatic with terrestrial as the two basic media of life, turning the adjective into a technical division.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学把 aquatic 与 terrestrial 配对为两种基本生活介质，使该形容词成为技术分类用语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the *akwa- base is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：*akwa- 词根属重构形式，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates aquatic from words built on the same aqua root but naming other things, and from one look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with neighbouring habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 aquatic 与同出 aqua 词根却指别物的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照相邻的栖息地词语。

entries.definition: A printmaking technique that mimics washes of tone; it is built on Italian acqua tinta 'tinted water', so it shares aqua but names no living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 一种模仿水墨浓淡的版画技法；由意大利语 acqua tinta「染色之水」构成，与 aqua 同源，却并不指生物。

entries.definition: A rock layer that holds groundwater; Latin aqua plus ferre 'to carry', so the water root is shared but the referent is stone, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 储存地下水的地层；由拉丁 aqua 加 ferre「携带」构成，水词根相同，所指却是岩层而非生命。

entries.definition: The farming of fish, shellfish and water plants; aqua plus cultura 'cultivation', so it names an industry rather than a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养殖鱼、贝类与水生植物；由 aqua 加 cultura「耕作」构成，指产业而非栖息地。

entries.definition: Hooked like an eagle's beak; it comes from Latin aquila 'eagle', not aqua 'water', so the resemblance is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 像鹰喙一样钩曲的；来自拉丁 aquila「鹰」而非 aqua「水」，因此形近并不同源。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to the sea; it is the salt-water half of aquatic and excludes rivers and lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在海中或与海有关的；它是 aquatic 的咸水一半，不含河流湖泊。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to non-salty inland water; it is the other half of aquatic, defined by low salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在淡水或与淡水有关的；是 aquatic 的另一半，以低盐度为界定。

entries.definition: Able to live both on land and in water; aquatic says one medium, amphibious adds the second.
entries.definitionCN: 能在陆地与水中两种环境生活；aquatic 只说一种介质，amphibious 则加上第二种。

entries.definition: Carried or spread by water, as a disease or a craft; it describes transport, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 由水携带或传播的，如疾病或船只；它描述运输，而非栖息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real aqua root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 aqua 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Aqua is Latin for water, and it survives in aquarium, aqueduct, aquifer and aquaculture.
normal.cn: aqua 是拉丁语的「水」，仍见于 aquarium、aqueduct、aquifer、aquaculture。

normal.en: The fixed pair aquatic / terrestrial divides life by medium in ecology textbooks.
normal.cn: 生态学教材用 aquatic / terrestrial 这一固定对立，按介质划分生命。

normal.en: Aquatic plants and aquatic animals are the two standard collocations in field guides.
normal.cn: aquatic plants 与 aquatic animals 是野外图鉴中的两个标准搭配。

normal.en: Aquatic sports is the administrative phrase for pool and lake events.
normal.cn: aquatic sports 是泳池与湖面赛事的行政管理用语。

normal.en: The noun aquatics names either water sports collectively or water-dwelling organisms.
normal.cn: 名词 aquatics 可指水上运动的总称，也可指水生生物。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf that lives half in air and half in water, its root never leaving the mud.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子一半在空气里、一半在水里，根始终不离开泥。

abstract.en: Picture a whole lake turned into a single room with its own weather.
abstract.cn: 想象整片湖被看成一间有自己天气的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer whose lines are so smooth that the water seems to move with her.
abstract.cn: 想象一位泳者的线条如此流畅，仿佛水随她而动。

examples.en: Aquatic plants filter the pond water and shelter young fish.
examples.cn: 水生植物过滤池水，也为幼鱼提供藏身处。

examples.en: The lake supports an aquatic community that changes with the seasons.
examples.cn: 这片湖养育着一个随季节变化的水生群落。

examples.en: She competes in three aquatic events at the national games.
examples.cn: 她在全国运动会上参加三个水上项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aqua（水）+ tic」——aqua 是水，加 -tic 成形容词：属于水的、活在水里的

root: 拉丁 aquaticus「生活在水中的」= aqua「水」+ -aticus（形容词后缀）；aqua 的印欧词根 *akwa- 为重构形式。英语 aquatic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one medium: water. The adjective first marks animals, then plants, then any condition or measurement set in water, then sports and tank keeping, then a technical ecological division; the noun simply names the organisms, and the last sense is a rare stylistic metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个介质「水」辐射开来：形容词先指动物，再指植物，随后指任何以水为场景的条件或测量、水上运动与水族饲养，再成为生态学的技术分类；名词直接指那类生物，最后一个义项是偶见的修辞隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life and activity whose whole setting is water.
core.cn: 核心意象：整个场景都泡在水里的生命与活动。

branches.en: LIVING IN WATER: animals and plants are labelled by the medium, not by shape.
branches.cn: 生于水中：动物与植物按介质而非体型被命名。

branches.en: WATER AS SETTING: measurements and ecological divisions treat water as the frame of study.
branches.cn: 以水为场景：测量与生态分类把水当作研究框架。

branches.en: SPORT IN WATER: the adjective becomes an administrative cover term for pool and lake events.
branches.cn: 水上运动：形容词成为泳池与湖面赛事的统称。

branches.en: THE ORGANISMS THEMSELVES: noun conversion names the life, including tank-kept life.
branches.cn: 生物本身：名词化后指这些生命，也包括水箱中饲养的。

branches.en: FLUID STYLE: the water image is borrowed for smooth motion, a marginal use.
branches.cn: 流畅风格：水的意象被借来形容平滑动作，属边缘用法。

intro.en: Aquatic is built from the Latin noun aqua plus the adjective suffix -aticus; the same root supplies a large family of water words in English.
intro.cn: aquatic 由拉丁名词 aqua 加形容词后缀 -aticus 构成；同一词根在英语中衍生出一大批与水有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aqua 'water' and its adjective aquaticus are the direct ancestors; aquarium and aquarius belong to the same word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aqua「水」及其形容词 aquaticus 是直接祖形；aquarium 与 aquarius 属于同一词族。

items.example: The aqua prefix marks water in technical terms.
items.exampleCN: aqua 前缀在技术术语中标记「水」。

items.example: Aquaticus means of water or living in water.
items.exampleCN: aquaticus 意为水的或生活在水中的。

items.example: Aquatic plants root below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 水生植物在水面下扎根。

items.example: The club runs aquatics for all ages.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部为各年龄层开设水上项目。

items.example: The larvae live aquatically before they emerge.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫出水前过水生生活。

items.meaning: a tank or building for water life
items.example: The aquarium holds native river fish.
The old aqueduct still carries spring water.
The aquifer supplies the whole valley.
Aquaculture now supplies half the fish sold.
items.exampleCN: 水产养殖如今供应售出鱼类的一半。

latinEntries.meaning: a watering place; a water container

definition_zh: 含水层；能够储存并输送地下水的透水岩层或沉积层
definition_en: a body of permeable rock or sediment that can store and transmit groundwater
core_image: 一层多孔的砂岩夹在两层致密泥岩之间，水在砂粒缝隙中缓慢横向流动
scene: 田边的钻井上，水泵把百尺之下砂层里的水抽上地面，农人接进灌溉渠。The pump lifts water from a sandstone aquifer far below the field.
sceneCN: 这里 aquifer 指「能储存并输送地下水的透水岩层」（第 1 个义项：由孔隙或裂隙透水、可作为地下水储库的岩层体）；句意为水泵把田地深处砂岩含水层中的水抽上来。可辨识物件：钻机、出水管、灌溉渠、砂岩层、泥岩隔水层。

senses.title: A water-bearing rock body
senses.titleCN: 含水岩层：能存水也能过水
senses.definition: a rock or sediment unit porous and permeable enough to hold and transmit usable amounts of water
senses.definitionCN: 孔隙与透水性足以储存并输送可用水量的岩层或沉积层
senses.example: The town draws its water from a shallow aquifer.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇子从一处浅层含水层取水。
senses.why: The word needs two conditions at once: enough empty space to store water, and enough connection between spaces to let it move toward a well.
senses.whyCN: 这个词同时要求两个条件：有足够空隙存水，且空隙彼此连通，让水能朝井的方向移动。

senses.title: The confined aquifer
senses.titleCN: 承压含水层：被隔水层压住
senses.definition: an aquifer lying between impermeable layers, so its water is under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 夹在不透水层之间、其中的水承受压力的含水层
senses.example: A confined aquifer can push water up a well without any pump.
senses.exampleCN: 承压含水层无需水泵就能把水顶到井口。
senses.why: If the water is sealed under a lid of clay, the weight upstream raises its pressure, and a well becomes a release valve.
senses.whyCN: 如果水被黏土层封在下面，上游的重力会提高它的压力，井口就成了泄压口。

senses.title: The unconfined aquifer
senses.definition: an aquifer whose upper limit is the water table, open to recharge from above
senses.definitionCN: 上界为潜水面、可接受上方补给的含水层
senses.example: In an unconfined aquifer the water level simply follows the water table.
senses.exampleCN: 在潜水含水层中，水位就随潜水面升降。
senses.why: With no lid, rain sinks straight in and the surface of the saturated zone is free to rise and fall with the seasons.
senses.whyCN: 没有盖子，雨水直接渗入，饱和带的水面便随季节自由升降。

senses.title: A source of supply
senses.titleCN: 供水水源：井与钻孔的对象
senses.definition: the underground layer that wells and boreholes are drilled into for supply
senses.definitionCN: 为供水而打井、钻孔所指向的地下岩层
senses.example: Farmers drilled into the aquifer to irrigate the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 农民钻入含水层为果园灌溉。
senses.why: Supply is not the water alone but the layer that yields it at a usable rate, so the layer itself becomes the resource in planning.
senses.whyCN: 供水不只是水本身，而是能以可用速率出水的那一层，因此在规划中这一层本身就成了资源。

senses.title: A hydrogeological unit
senses.titleCN: 水文地质单元：图上的一块
senses.definition: a mapped unit with defined boundaries, properties and flow behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 具有确定边界、性质与流动行为并可在图上标出的单元
senses.example: The model divides the basin into four aquifer units.
senses.exampleCN: 模型把这个流域分成四个含水层单元。
senses.why: Once the layer is given boundaries and numbers, it stops being a place and becomes a unit that can be modelled and assigned rights.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这一层被划定边界并赋以数值，它就不再只是一个地方，而成为可模拟、可分配权利的单元。

senses.title: Storage and recharge
senses.titleCN: 储水与回灌：把水放回去
senses.definition: the layer used to bank water underground for later recovery
senses.definitionCN: 用于把水存到地下、日后取回的那一层
senses.example: The city injects treated storm water into the aquifer each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市每年冬天把处理过的雨水注入含水层。
senses.why: If the rock already holds water, it can also hold more; the aquifer becomes a bank with slow deposits and faster withdrawals.
senses.whyCN: 如果岩层本来就能存水，它也能存更多；含水层于是成了一家存款慢、取款快的银行。

senses.title: Vulnerability to pollution
senses.titleCN: 污染脆弱性：容易被弄脏的储库
senses.definition: an aquifer considered in terms of how easily contaminants reach and persist in it
senses.definitionCN: 从污染物进入与滞留难易程度来看的含水层
senses.example: The shallow aquifer is vulnerable to nitrate from the fields above.
senses.exampleCN: 浅层含水层容易受到上方农田硝酸盐的影响。
senses.why: A porous layer with a thin cover admits pollution quickly and cleans it slowly, so vulnerability becomes a property of the layer itself.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖薄而多孔的岩层让污染进得快、清得慢，因此脆弱性成了这一层自身的属性。

senses.title: Abstract: a deep reserve
senses.definition: any large hidden store that can be drawn on over time
senses.definitionCN: 任何可长期取用的巨大隐藏储备
senses.example: The archive is an aquifer of forgotten detail for the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 对历史学者而言，这座档案馆是一座被遗忘细节的深藏水库。
senses.why: The image keeps its key features: invisible, capacious, slowly refilled, and easy to drain without noticing.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象保留了关键特征：看不见、容量大、补充缓慢，而且在不知不觉中容易被抽干。

intro.en: Aquifer is a learned Latin coinage, not an inherited word: aqua supplies water and -fer supplies bearing. It entered English through geology in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: aquifer 是学术性的拉丁语新造词，而非承继词：aqua 提供「水」，-fer 提供「承载」。它在十九世纪经地质学进入英语。

items.en: Aqua was the ordinary Latin word for water and survives in aquarium, aquatic and aqueduct; it is a different root from Greek hydōr.
items.cn: aqua 是拉丁语中表示水的普通词，留存于 aquarium、aquatic 与 aqueduct；它与希腊语 hydōr 是不同的词根。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and its combining form -fer appears in many scientific adjectives such as carboniferous and coniferous.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带、承载，其组合形式 -fer 出现在许多科学形容词中，如 carboniferous 与 coniferous。

items.en: The compound is generally regarded as a modern Latin formation in which the two Latin elements were joined to name a water-bearing stratum.
items.cn: 这个复合词一般被认为是近代拉丁语构词，把两个拉丁成分组合起来，用于命名含水岩层。

items.en: English geology adopted aquifer in the early nineteenth century, when groundwater stopped being described simply as water in wells and became a layer with properties.
items.cn: 英国地质学在十九世纪初采纳 aquifer，当时地下水不再只被描述为井中之水，而成为具有性质的一层。

items.en: Source uncertain (coiner and first date): the exact author and year of the first use of aquifer are not fixed in standard dictionaries, so the dating here is an estimate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首创者与首见年代）：aquifer 首次使用的确切作者与年份在通行辞书中未定，此处的年代只是估计。

note.en: The first group holds the Latin-shaped neighbours that are easiest to confuse; the second holds the layers and water bodies that are close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是最易混淆的拉丁词形近邻；第二组是含义相近的岩层与水体。

entries.definition: A channel or bridge built to convey water; the second element means 'lead', not 'bear'.
entries.definitionCN: 为输水而建的渠道或渡槽；第二个成分意为「引导」，不是「承载」。

entries.definition: Water as a Latin word and a combining form; it is one piece of aquifer, not another kind of layer.
entries.definitionCN: 作为拉丁词与组合成分的「水」；它是 aquifer 的一个构件，而不是另一类岩层。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'water-bearing'; it describes a layer rather than naming one.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「含水的」形容词；它描述岩层，而不给岩层命名。

entries.definition: A layer that holds water but will not transmit it; the second element means 'shut'.
entries.definitionCN: 能含水却不导水的岩层；第二个成分意为「关闭」。

entries.definition: The water inside the layer; an aquifer is the container and groundwater is what it holds.
entries.definitionCN: 岩层中的水；含水层是容器，地下水是所装之物。

entries.definition: A bed that blocks flow and therefore defines the boundaries of an aquifer.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止水流、因而界定含水层边界的岩层。

entries.definition: Any natural or artificial store of water; only the aquifer is specifically a rock layer.
entries.definitionCN: 任何天然或人工的储水体；只有含水层特指岩层。

entries.definition: The top surface of the saturated zone, not the layer that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 饱和带的上表面，而不是包含它的岩层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the pair with aquiclude, and the pressure difference between the two aquifer types.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、与 aquiclude 的成对关系，以及两类含水层的压力差别。

normal.en: aqua is water, -fer is bearing: an aquifer is literally a water-bearer.
normal.cn: aqua 是水，-fer 是承载：aquifer 字面就是「载水者」。

normal.en: aquiclude has -clude, to shut: the layer that shuts water out, the exact opposite of the aquifer.
normal.cn: aquiclude 含 -clude「关闭」：把水关在外面的岩层，正好与含水层相反。

normal.en: Confined means a lid of impermeable rock; unconfined means no lid at all.
normal.cn: confined 表示有不透水岩层做盖；unconfined 表示完全没有盖。

normal.en: An aquifer stores and transmits; a tank stores only. That is why the word needs both pore space and connection.
normal.cn: 含水层既储存又输送，水箱只储存；所以这个词同时要求孔隙空间与连通性。

normal.en: The adjective is aquiferous, so the geology family keeps the Latin -fer throughout.
normal.cn: 形容词是 aquiferous，地质学词族始终保留拉丁的 -fer。

abstract.en: Abstractly, an aquifer is a sponge made of stone: the rock is the solid, the water is the content, and the pores are the roads.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，含水层是一块石头做的海绵：岩石是固体，水是内容，孔隙是道路。

abstract.en: It is also a slow bank: deposits arrive by gravity over years, withdrawals happen in minutes.
abstract.cn: 它也是一家缓慢的银行：存款靠重力经年累月到达，取款却只需几分钟。

abstract.en: Any system that hides capacity inside solid structure follows this model — including institutions and memory.
abstract.cn: 任何把容量藏在坚固结构内部的系统都遵循这个模型——包括制度与记忆。

examples.en: The aquifer under the plain holds enough water for a century of farming.
examples.cn: 平原下的含水层储存的水足够农业用一百年。

examples.en: Salt water has crept into the coastal aquifer as pumping lowered its pressure.
examples.cn: 抽水降低了压力，海水因此侵入沿海含水层。

examples.en: Geologists map an aquifer by measuring how easily water moves through the rock.
examples.cn: 地质学家通过测量水穿过岩石的难易程度来绘制含水层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夸（aqua，水）+ 弗（-fer，带着）」——带着水的那层石头 → 含水层

root: 拉丁语 aqua「水」+ -fer（ferre「携带、承载」），近代拉丁语新造词，十九世纪进入英语地质学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one layer: the rock that holds and moves water, its two pressure types, its use as supply, its status as a mapped unit, its banking and pollution, and finally its use as an image of a deep reserve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一岩层展开：能存水也能过水的岩层、两种压力类型、作为供水对象、作为图上单元、储水回灌与污染，最后是作为「深处储备」的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a porous sandstone bed between two tight clay beds, water creeping sideways through the sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：夹在两层致密黏土之间的多孔砂岩层，水在砂粒间横向缓行。

branches.en: TWO CONDITIONS: storage space plus connected pores make a rock an aquifer.
branches.cn: 两个条件：储水空间加上连通的孔隙，才使岩层成为含水层。

branches.en: WITH OR WITHOUT A LID: pressure or freedom at the top separates the two types.
branches.cn: 有盖或无盖：顶部受压还是自由，区分了两种类型。

branches.en: THE WELL: supply is the layer yielding water at a usable rate.
branches.cn: 井：供水指的是以可用速率出水的那一层。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES AND RISK: mapped units have edges, and edges admit pollution.
branches.cn: 边界与风险：被制图的单元有边界，而边界会放进污染。

branches.en: BANK AND METAPHOR: water can be deposited underground, and the same image serves any hidden capacity.
branches.cn: 银行与比喻：水可以存到地下，而同一意象可用于任何隐藏容量。

intro.en: Aquifer is built from two Latin morphemes that also build a visible technical family, so the word can be read from its parts.
intro.cn: aquifer 由两个拉丁语素构成，这两个语素还构成一个可见的技术词族，因此可以从构件读出词义。

latinIntro.en: The Latin basis is aqua, water, and ferre, to bear. The same two elements recur in aquiferous and in the contrasting aquiclude, where claudere, to shut, replaces ferre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 aqua「水」与 ferre「承载」。同样两个成分也见于 aquiferous，以及与之相对、以 claudere「关闭」替换 ferre 的 aquiclude。

items.example: The aquifer supplies the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 这个含水层供养整个谷地。

items.example: The aquiferous sandstone is drilled for water.
items.exampleCN: 人们在这层含水砂岩中钻井取水。

items.meaning: a layer that holds but does not transmit water
items.meaningCN: 能含水却不导水的岩层
items.example: Clay forms an aquiclude above the sand.
items.exampleCN: 黏土在砂层之上形成隔水层。

items.meaning: a channel built to carry water
items.example: The old aqueduct still crosses the valley.
items.exampleCN: 古老的渡槽仍横跨谷地。

items.example: Aquaculture supplies much of the world's fish.
items.exampleCN: 水产养殖提供世界上很大一部分鱼。
水生昆虫占据了这口池塘。

definition_zh: adj. 可耕的，适于耕种的（土地）　n. 耕地；种植业
definition_en: Of land, suitable for ploughing and growing crops rather than for pasture or trees; as a noun, arable land or crop farming.
core_image: 犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地
scene: 这一带只剩三成土地还能耕种。Only thirty per cent of the land here is arable.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arable 修饰土地，指能犁能种庄稼，与牧场、林地相对。

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（分类性形容词）

senses.title: Land that can be ploughed
senses.definition: of soil or a field, in a condition that allows ploughing and the growing of crops
senses.definitionCN: 指土壤或田地的状况允许犁耕并种植作物
senses.example: The valley holds the only arable soil for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 方圆数英里只有这个山谷有可耕的土壤。
senses.why: The Latin root means plough and -able means able to be, so arable literally says able to be ploughed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「犁」，-able 意为「可被……的」，所以 arable 字面就是「犁得动的」。

senses.title: Crop farming as a category
senses.definition: in British farming use, arable land or arable as a noun, the branch of agriculture that grows crops rather than raising animals
senses.definitionCN: 英式农业用语中作名词，指种庄稼而非养牲畜的那一支农业
senses.example: The farm switched from dairy to arable in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场九十年代从奶牛转向了种植。
senses.why: Once the adjective named a kind of land, it could stand for that kind of farming, so the quality word became a category word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词一旦指某类土地，就能进而指那类农业，于是表性质的词变成了表类别的词。

intro.en: Arable is Latin arabilis, that can be ploughed, from arare, to plough. The same ancient root gives Old English erian, to plough, and Greek arotos.
intro.cn: arable 就是拉丁语 arabilis「可犁的」，来自 arare「犁地」。同一古老词根还产生古英语 erian「犁」与希腊语 arotos。

items.en: The reconstructed root ar- meant to plough, one of the oldest farming words in the Indo-European family.
items.cn: 重构词根 ar- 意为「犁」，是印欧语系中最古老的农事词之一。

items.en: Latin arare meant to plough a field, the physical act of turning the soil with a blade.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arare 意为「犁田」，即用犁刀翻土这一实际动作。

items.en: Adding -abilis, able to be, gave arabilis, of land that will take the plough.
items.cn: 加上 -abilis「可被……的」得到 arabilis，指能吃得住犁的土地。

items.en: Old English erian, to plough, is the native cousin, which shows the root reached both branches.
items.cn: 古英语 erian「犁」是本族同源词，说明这个词根传到了两大支系。

items.en: French arable carried the Latin adjective into medieval Europe unchanged in shape and sense.
items.cn: 法语 arable 把这个拉丁形容词带入中世纪欧洲，形与义都没变。

items.en: English recorded arable in the fifteenth century, and British farming later made it a noun for crop growing.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪记录到 arable，后来英国农业把它用作指种植业的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against arid, which is the opposite kind of land, and parable, which only sounds similar; the near-meaning group gives other words for farmable ground.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与表示相反地况的 arid、以及只是音似的 parable 混淆；近义组给出其他表示可耕地的词。

normalIntro.en: Arable is ar-, plough, plus -able: land the plough can get through.
normalIntro.cn: arable 就是 ar-「犁」加 -able「能……的」：犁能翻得动的地。

normal.en: The fixed pair is arable land, opposed to pasture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 arable land，与 pasture 相对。

normal.en: Do not confuse arable with arid, which means dry.
normal.cn: 别把 arable 与 arid「干旱的」混淆。

normal.en: Arable farming grows crops; dairy farming keeps cows.
normal.cn: arable farming 种庄稼，dairy farming 养奶牛。

normal.en: There is no comparative: land is arable or it is not.
normal.cn: 没有比较级：地要么可耕，要么不可耕。

normal.en: In British use arable alone can be a noun.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 arable 可单独作名词。

abstract.en: Picture a blade turning dark soil in a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象犁刀把黑土翻成一条直线。

abstract.en: Imagine a map shaded only where crops can grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只在能种庄稼处上色的地图。

abstract.en: Think of stony ground that stops the plough dead.
abstract.cn: 想象让犁当场卡住的石质地。

examples.en: Erosion has cut the arable area by a fifth.
examples.cn: 侵蚀使可耕面积减少了五分之一。

examples.en: The village lost its arable land to the new road.
examples.cn: 村里的耕地被新建公路占去了。

examples.en: They grow wheat on every arable field they have.
examples.cn: 他们在每一块可耕的田里都种小麦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ar-「犁」+ -able「能……的」——犁得动、种得出粮，就是可耕的 arable。

root: 原始印欧词根 ar-「犁」生出拉丁 arare「犁地」，加 -abilis 成 arabilis「可犁的」，经法语进入英语作 arable；古英语 erian 与希腊 arotos 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses follow the plough: land the plough can enter, and the kind of farming that lives on such land.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都跟着犁走：犁能进得去的地，以及靠这种地吃饭的那类农业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the plot the plough can turn and crops can come out of
core.cn: 核心意象：犁能翻得动、种得出粮的那片地

branches.en: A valley of dark ploughable soil.
Stony ground the blade cannot enter.
A farm switching from cows to wheat.
branches.cn: 从养牛转种小麦的农场。

branches.en: Arable as a branch of agriculture.
branches.cn: 作为农业一支的种植业。

branches.en: Both are defined by the plough.

intro.en: Arable is the plough root ar- plus -able; the field root agr- builds agriculture and agrarian beside it.
intro.cn: arable 是「犁」词根 ar- 加 -able；旁边的「田」词根 agr- 构成 agriculture 与 agrarian。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arare, arabilis, ager, a field, and colere, to till, which gives cultivate and culture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arare、arabilis、ager「田地」与 colere「耕作」，后者产生 cultivate 与 culture。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arare 是 arable 的来源。

definition_zh: 任意的；随意的；专断的；武断的
definition_en: based on personal choice rather than reason, or using power without limits
core_image: 裁判随手一指，全凭个人喜好
scene: 规则没有写明，全凭他一句话决定。The choice of colour seemed arbitrary rather than planned.
sceneCN: 这里 arbitrary 是「随意的」（第 1 个义项：出于个人选择而非理由）；句意是颜色的选择看上去是随手定的，而非事先规划。

derivatives.zh: 动词：仲裁，同出 arbiter 一词

senses.title: Chosen at random
senses.definition: decided by personal whim rather than by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 凭个人一时喜好决定，而非依据规则
senses.example: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。
senses.why: Latin arbitrarius described whatever depended on the will of an arbiter, so the word began as 'left to choice'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arbitrarius 指「取决于仲裁者意志的」，所以这个词一开始就是「交由选择决定」的意思。

senses.title: Using power without restraint
senses.definition: acting on will alone, with no check from law or others
senses.definitionCN: 只凭意志行事，不受法律或他人约束
senses.example: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
senses.exampleCN: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。
senses.why: When the will belongs to a person with power, 'left to choice' turns into 'answerable to nobody', which is the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 当这种意志属于掌权者时，「交由选择」就变成「不受任何人约束」，这就是政治上的专断义。

intro.en: Arbitrary comes from the Latin word for a judge who decides by his own will.
intro.cn: arbitrary 源自拉丁语中表示「凭自己意志裁决的法官」的词。

items.en: arbiter meant 'judge, witness, one who decides'.
items.cn: arbiter 意为「法官、见证人、裁决者」。

items.en: arbitrium meant 'judgment, will, choice'.
items.cn: arbitrium 意为「判断、意志、选择」。

items.en: arbitrarius meant 'depending on the will'.
items.cn: arbitrarius 意为「取决于意志的」。

items.en: English borrowed it for decisions resting on mere will.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指仅凭意志作出的决定。

items.en: The sense widened from one judge's will to any unchecked power.
items.cn: 词义从一位法官的意志扩展到任何不受制约的权力。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same judge root; the near-meaning group gives other words for will without reason.
note.cn: 形近组同出「裁决者」词根；近义组是其他表示无理性凭意志的词。

normalIntro.en: Arbitrary means the will decides and nothing else does.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrary 意为只由意志决定，别无其他依据。

normal.en: A judge called an arbiter gave the word its root.
normal.cn: 名为 arbiter 的裁决者给了它词根。

normal.en: Arbitrary rules are the opposite of measured ones.
normal.cn: arbitrary 的规定与有依据的规定相反。

normal.en: The adverb is arbitrarily, often used in complaints.
normal.cn: 副词 arbitrarily 常用于抱怨的语境。

normal.en: Arbitration keeps the same root but means fair judging.
normal.cn: arbitration 同根，却表示公平裁断。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-bi-tra-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-bi-tra-ry。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing at one name without reason.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指毫无理由地点中一个名字。

abstract.en: See a ruler's hand signing without reading.
abstract.cn: 想象掌权者不看内容就签字。

abstract.en: See dice thrown to settle a question.
abstract.cn: 想象掷骰子来决定一个问题。

examples.en: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
examples.cn: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。

examples.en: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
examples.cn: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。

examples.en: Critics called the deadline arbitrary and unfair.
examples.cn: 批评者称这个期限既武断又不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: arbiter（裁决者）加 -ary：裁决者想怎么定就怎么定，于是成了随意的、专断的。

root: 来自拉丁语 arbitrarius「取决于意志的」，源自动词 arbiter「裁决者」与 arbitrium「判断、意志」；由「凭裁决者意志」引申出随意与专断两义。

sensesIntro.en: One root covers both a casual choice and a ruler who answers to no one.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根既涵盖随手的选择，也涵盖不受约束的掌权者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to point at one option out of many.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在众多选项里随手点向其中一个。

branches.en: an arbitrary choice
arbitrary order
arbitrary power
arbitrary arrests
an arbitrary standard

intro.en: A word about will and judgment that split into fairness and its opposite.
intro.cn: 这个词讲的是意志与判断，后来既生出公正，也生出不公。

latinIntro.en: The root arbiter, 'judge', also gives arbitrate and arbitration.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 arbiter「裁决者」也派生出 arbitrate 与 arbitration。

items.meaning: able to be settled by a judge

definition_zh: n. 仲裁，公断（由中立第三方裁断争议）；（合同中的）仲裁机制
definition_en: The settlement of a dispute by an independent third party whose decision the sides have agreed to accept; in contracts, the mechanism that replaces going to court.
core_image: 双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板
scene: 合同写明争议一律提交仲裁。The contract sends every dispute to arbitration.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitration 指把争议交给中立第三方裁断，而不是上法院。

senses.title: Settlement by a third party
senses.definition: the process in which a neutral person or panel hears both sides and issues a decision that resolves the dispute
senses.definitionCN: 由中立个人或小组听取双方陈述并作出解决争议的裁定的程序
senses.example: The pay dispute ended in arbitration after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周之后，薪酬争议以仲裁收场。
senses.why: The root arbiter means one who goes to see and judge, so arbitration is literally the work of that witness turned judge.
senses.whyCN: 词根 arbiter 意为「去看并作出判断的人」，所以 arbitration 字面就是那位见证人转为裁判后所做的工作。

senses.title: The contractual mechanism
senses.definition: in law and commerce, the agreed route that replaces litigation, usually written into a contract as a clause
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与商业中，指替代诉讼的约定途径，通常以条款形式写进合同
senses.example: Binding arbitration bars either side from suing later.
senses.exampleCN: 有约束力的仲裁禁止任何一方事后起诉。
senses.why: Here the word names an institution rather than an event: the standing arrangement the parties chose before any quarrel began.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是一套制度而非一次事件：双方在争吵开始之前就选好的常设安排。

intro.en: Arbitration comes from Latin arbitratio, from arbitrari, to judge, from arbiter, a witness who goes to see, built from ad-, to, and baetere, to come.
intro.cn: arbitration 来自拉丁语 arbitratio，出自 arbitrari「裁断」，而 arbitrari 来自 arbiter「去看情况的见证人」，由 ad-「向」与 baetere「来、去」构成。

items.en: Latin arbiter named someone who goes to look at a matter and then judges it, a witness with authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arbiter 指去查看某事然后作出判断的人，一个有权威的见证人。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to consider and decide, at first neutrally, without any hint of whim.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「考量并裁定」，起初是中性的，没有任何「随意」的意味。

items.en: The noun arbitratio named the act of judging between parties, the source of the modern term.
items.cn: 名词 arbitratio 指在各方之间裁断这一行为，是现代术语的来源。

items.en: Old French kept arbitration for settlement out of court, a practice medieval merchants relied on.
items.cn: 古法语用 arbitration 指庭外解决，这是中世纪商人依赖的做法。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century for the decision of an arbitrator.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪记录该词，指仲裁人作出的裁定。

items.en: Today arbitration clauses sit in trade and labour contracts, and the award is enforceable across borders.
items.cn: 如今仲裁条款见于贸易与劳动合同，裁决可跨境执行。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts arbitrary, which is whim rather than reasoned judgement, and arbitrage, a trading term; the near-meaning group lists other ways to settle a dispute.
note.cn: 形近组对比 arbitrary「凭兴致而非讲理裁断」与 arbitrage「套利」；近义组列出其他解决争议的方式。

A person with power to decide.
Profiting from price gaps between markets.
Helping sides reach their own deal.

An agreement that ends a dispute.

normalIntro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation: the work of the person who comes, looks and decides.
normalIntro.cn: arbitration 就是 arbiter 加 -ation：那位「来看一看再拍板」的人所做的工作。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say arbitration, not an arbitration.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 arbitration，不说 an arbitration。

normal.en: The person is an arbitrator; the verb is arbitrate.
normal.cn: 人是 arbitrator，动词是 arbitrate。

normal.en: Arbitrary means capricious, a very different judgement.
normal.cn: arbitrary 意为反复无常，是完全不同的评价。

normal.en: Mediation helps sides agree; arbitration decides for them.
normal.cn: mediation 帮双方谈成，arbitration 替他们定。

normal.en: The result is called an award, not a verdict.
normal.cn: 结果叫 award，不叫 verdict。

abstract.en: Picture two people pointing at one line on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两人指着地图上同一条线争执。

abstract.en: Imagine a third chair placed between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象在争执双方之间摆上第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Think of a contract that quietly rules out court.
abstract.cn: 想象一份悄悄排除法院的合同。

examples.en: Both firms agreed to settle by arbitration.
examples.cn: 两家公司同意通过仲裁解决。

examples.en: The arbitration clause survives the rest of the contract.
examples.cn: 仲裁条款在合同其余部分失效后仍然有效。

examples.en: Arbitration is usually faster than a court case.
examples.cn: 仲裁通常比诉讼快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbiter「裁判」+ -ation「行为」——请裁判来断案，就是仲裁 arbitration。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」成 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」，生出 arbitrari「裁断」与 arbitratio；经古法语入英语作 arbitration，指庭外裁断。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one act of judging: the hearing that settles a quarrel, and the standing arrangement that promises such a hearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种裁断：解决争吵的那次听审，以及承诺会有这种听审的常设安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides talking past each other, one person in the middle deciding
core.cn: 核心意象：双方各说各话，交给中间那个人拍板

branches.en: A pay quarrel closed in six weeks.
A panel hearing both sides once.
branches.cn: 一次性听取双方的小组。

branches.en: A clause that rules out court.
An award enforceable abroad.
Both put the decision in a third hand.
branches.cn: 两者都把裁定交到第三方手里。

intro.en: Arbitration is arbiter plus -ation; the same root builds arbitrate, arbitrator, arbitral, arbitrary and arbitrage.
intro.cn: arbitration 是 arbiter 加 -ation；同一词根还构成 arbitrate、arbitrator、arbitral、arbitrary 与 arbitrage。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and arbitratio; the prefix inside arbiter is ad-, to, before baetere, to come.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与 arbitratio；arbiter 内部的前缀是 ad-「向」，接 baetere「来」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arbitrari 是 arbitration 的来源。

definition_zh: n. 仲裁人，公断人；（引申）最终裁定者
definition_en: An independent person appointed to hear a dispute and give a decision that the parties have agreed to accept; by extension, anyone whose judgement settles a question.
core_image: 坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人
scene: 双方各让一步，接受了仲裁人的裁定。Both sides accepted the arbitrator's ruling.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitrator 指被指定来听审并裁断争议的中立第三方。

pos.zh: 仲裁人；公断人；最终裁定者

senses.title: The appointed decider
senses.definition: a neutral person chosen by the parties, or by a body, to hear evidence and impose a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 由双方或某机构选定的中立者，听取证据并作出有约束力的解决方案
senses.example: The union and the firm could not agree on an arbitrator.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与公司无法就仲裁人人选达成一致。
senses.why: The ending -or marks the doer, so arbitrator is simply the one who arbitrates, the person inside the process.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -or 标记施动者，所以 arbitrator 就是「做仲裁的那个人」，是程序里的那个人。

senses.title: The final authority on a question
senses.definition: by extension, a person or thing whose judgement is treated as settling a matter of taste or value
senses.definitionCN: 引申指其判断被视为能定论品味或价值问题的人或事物
senses.example: Time is the only arbitrator of literary reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是文学声誉唯一的裁定者。
senses.why: The legal role is borrowed as a metaphor: whoever ends the argument occupies the middle chair, even with no contract.
senses.whyCN: 法律角色被借作比喻：谁能终止争论，谁就坐上了中间那把椅子，哪怕并无合同。

intro.en: Arbitrator is the Latin agent noun from arbitrari, to judge, itself from arbiter, a witness who goes to see. English took both arbiter and arbitrator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是拉丁语 arbitrari「裁断」的施动名词，而 arbitrari 出自 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」。英语把 arbiter 与 arbitrator 都吸收了。

items.en: Arbiter meant a witness who goes to look and then judges, from ad-, to, plus baetere, to come.
items.cn: arbiter 指前去看情况再作判断的见证人，由 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」构成。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to weigh a matter and decide it, the neutral ancestor of both English words.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「权衡并裁定」，是两个英语词的中性祖先。

items.en: Adding -or, the doer ending, gave arbitrator, the person who performs the judging.
items.cn: 加上表施动者的 -or 得到 arbitrator，即执行裁断的那个人。

items.en: Anglo-French legal writing spelled it arbitratour, the form English courts used in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语法律文献拼作 arbitratour，这是 14 世纪末英国法院使用的形式。

items.en: English kept both forms: arbiter for any decisive authority, arbitrator for the appointed legal role.
items.cn: 英语保留了两种形式：arbiter 泛指有定论权的权威，arbitrator 专指被指定的法律角色。

items.en: Today an arbitrator is named in the clause, and the award carries the force of a court judgement.
items.cn: 如今仲裁人在条款中被指定，其裁决具有法院判决的效力。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arbiter, the wider word, from arbitrator, the appointed role, and warns against arbitrary; the near-meaning group lists other neutral deciders.
note.cn: 形近组把泛指的 arbiter 与专任的 arbitrator 分开，并提醒别与 arbitrary 混淆；近义组列出其他中立裁断者。

entries.definition: A person who gives a formal ruling.
An official who enforces the rules.
One who judges value or quality.

normalIntro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus -or: the person who does the arbitrating, sitting in the middle chair.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrator 就是 arbitrate 加 -or：做仲裁的那个人，坐在中间那把椅子上。

normal.en: Arbitrator is the appointed role; arbiter is the wider word.
normal.cn: arbitrator 是专任角色，arbiter 是泛指说法。

normal.en: A mediator only helps; an arbitrator decides.
normal.cn: mediator 只帮谈，arbitrator 直接定。

normal.en: The decision is an award, and it binds the parties.
normal.cn: 裁定叫 award，对双方有约束力。

normal.en: Sole arbitrator means one person, not a panel.
normal.cn: sole arbitrator 指独任一人，不是小组。

normal.en: Do not mix arbitrator with arbitrary, which means capricious.
normal.cn: 别把 arbitrator 与 arbitrary「反复无常」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a third chair between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象争执双方之间的第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a signature that ends a two-year quarrel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名结束两年争吵。

abstract.en: Think of time as the judge nobody appointed.
abstract.cn: 想象时间这位没人指定的裁判。

examples.en: The arbitrator heard both sides for three days.
examples.cn: 仲裁人听双方陈述听了三天。

examples.en: Two arbitrators were replaced for a conflict of interest.
examples.cn: 两名仲裁人因利益冲突被更换。

examples.en: She acted as sole arbitrator in the shipping dispute.
examples.cn: 她在这起航运争议中担任独任仲裁人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbitrate「仲裁」+ -or「人」——做仲裁的那个人，就是 arbitrator。

root: 拉丁语 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」生出 arbitrari「裁断」，加施动后缀 -or 成 arbitrator「裁断者」；英语 14 世纪末吸收，与泛指的 arbiter 分工并存。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the middle chair: the person appointed to end a dispute, and anyone whose word ends an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是中间那把椅子：被指定来终结争议的人，以及一句话就能终结争论的任何人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person seated between the two sides who makes the final call
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人

branches.en: A neutral named in the clause.
Three days of hearing both sides.
Time judging literary reputation.
A critic whose word ends debate.
branches.cn: 一句话终止争论的评论家。

branches.en: Both occupy the middle chair.
branches.cn: 两者都坐在中间那把椅子上。

intro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus the doer suffix -or, the same ending that builds actor, mediator and adjudicator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是 arbitrate 加施动后缀 -or，同一词尾还构成 actor、mediator 与 adjudicator。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and the agent noun arbitrator; -or is the Latin doer ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与施动名词 arbitrator；-or 是拉丁语的施动者词尾。

latinEntries.example: Arbiter is the base of the family.
